claims.claim: Lake Simoncouche, Québec, is shallow: 83 ha, mean depth 2.2 m
claims.location: web page, Methods, 'Study site and zooplankton community'
claims.quote: mean depth 2.2 m, maximum depth 8 m and surface area 83 ha
claims.conditions: 48°23′N, 71°25′W; mesotrophic; ice from November to late April or early May, ice up to 50–90 cm thick; no hypolimnion forms

claims.claim: annual mean densities: L. minutus 12.9/L, Daphnia 4.9/L, Cyclops scutifer 3.3/L
claims.location: web page, Results, 'Seasonal abundances in zooplankton community'
claims.quote: average annual abundances of 12.9 ± 4.9, 3.3 ± 1.7 and 4.9 ± 2.8 ind
claims.conditions: listed in the order L. minutus, C. scutifer, Daphnia spp. (mean ± SD, ind/L); copepodites and adults together; weekly to monthly samples, 19 May 2011 – 23 May 2012; 58 %, 15 % and 22 % of total community abundance
claims.note: The paper's mapping is right: 4.9 is Daphnia's mean (and, by coincidence, L. minutus's SD). 'Daphnia' is Daphnia spp.

claims.claim: M. edax 1.0/L, absent from November to May
claims.location: web page, Results, 'Seasonal abundances in zooplankton community'
claims.quote: Mesocyclops edax was absent from the water column from November to May
claims.conditions: 1.0 ± 1.1 ind/L, 5 % of the annual community; it spends that period in the sediments as C-V copepodites (Discussion)

claims.claim: L. minutus lipid rose from 18 % of dry weight in September to 76 % in January
claims.location: web page, Results, 'Total lipids and fatty acid composition in zooplankton'
claims.quote: lipid content ranged from 18% (of dry weight) in mid-September to 76% in late January

claims.claim: starved adults at 4 °C survived as well as fed ones for 66 days before collapsing
claims.location: web page, Results, 'Starvation experiment'; Methods, 'Survival experiment'
claims.quote: During the first 66 days of the experiment, the survival was not significantly different
claims.conditions: laboratory, 4 °C in the dark; adult L. minutus collected at freeze-up (20 Nov 2012); 6 beakers × 50 copepods per treatment; starved = GF/F-filtered lake water, fed = < 50-µm lake water, renewed weekly. From day 66 to day 73 the starved survivors fell from 32 ± 6 to 3 ± 2; on day 163, 0.2 ± 0.4 starved against 21 ± 7 fed were alive

claims.claim: copepod adults live months and overwinter on lipid (L. minutus)
claims.location: web page, Results ('Seasonal abundances'; 'Total lipids'); Discussion
claims.quote: minutus spent the winter as an adult
claims.conditions: L. minutus overwintered as adults and stored lipid to 76 % of dry weight; the stored lipid alone lasted about two months (66 d) in the laboratory, and phytoplankton fatty acids stayed available in the lake for about a month after ice-on
claims.note: The authors' point is that the copepod 'does not survive five months under the ice without food' (Abstract): it overwinters on lipid built from early-winter phytoplankton plus some winter feeding, not on lipid alone. The loss rate of ~0.0005/day in the comment is Cooley's (1973), not from this paper.

notes: Every value checks. Also useful: Daphnia in Lake Simoncouche were mostly adults under the ice, fairly abundant until 12 December and then scarce until mid-May; C. scutifer overwintered entirely as C-IV copepodites; Bosmina was abundant in early winter. Under-ice chlorophyll a was 0.2–0.7 µg/L against 1.4–3.5 µg/L in the open season (Table 1). L. minutus can make up 93 % of the zooplankton biomass (Grosbois, unpublished, cited in Methods).
